newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Eletrobras plans level 3 ADR.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Eletrobras plans level 3 ADR.

text.p: Brazil's state-owned power firm Eletrobras plans to launch Level Three American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), possibly as early as next year, a company official said.
"We plan to issue level three ADRs. First we intend to seek bids to hire a consultant to bring our books in line with U.S. standards," a company official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.
Eletrobras, which plans to launch the issue a year after hiring the consultant, already is traded over the counter in the U.S. as a Level One ADR.
"We're going to jump from Level One directly to Level Three," said the source, adding the company does not intend to issue Level Two ADRs.
The source said neither the size of the issue nor the launch date had not been determined yet, but the company planned to hire a consultant "soon."

Eletrobras, whose major assets are to be privatized piecemeal starting at the end of 1997, is the holding company for the federal eletrical power system and accounts for 48 percent of Brazil's power generating capacity.
It controls six subsidiaries. Furnas, Eletronorte, Eletrosul, Chesf are responsible for hydropower; Nuclen manages nuclear power; and Lightpar is Eletrobras's investment arm.
The government so far has privatized two power distributors, Light and Escelsa, which are not part of the Eletrobras system.
